text: Fill in the blanks: For a particular reaction, the rate constant is 0.05 s⁻¹. The reaction is of ______ order and will be ______ of the initial concentration.
explanation: The unit s⁻¹ shows a first-order rate constant. For a first-order reaction, the half-life (0.693/k) does not depend on the initial concentration.

text: Fill in the blanks: EDTA is used in the treatment of ______ while cisplatin is used in the treatment of ______.
explanation: EDTA chelates Pb²⁺ ions, removing lead from the body. Cisplatin, [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], is an anticancer drug.

text: Fill in the blanks: Adding a small quantity of ethanol to chloroform prevents the formation of ______ and converts it into the harmless compound ______.
explanation: Chloroform is oxidised by air in light to poisonous phosgene (COCl₂). Ethanol converts any phosgene formed into harmless diethyl carbonate: COCl₂ + 2C₂H₅OH → (C₂H₅O)₂CO + 2HCl.

text: Fill in the blanks: Dehydration of ethyl alcohol with conc. H₂SO₄ at 140 °C mainly yields ______, while at 170 °C the main product is ______.
explanation: At 413 K (140 °C, excess alcohol) intermolecular dehydration gives diethyl ether; at 443 K (170 °C, excess acid) intramolecular dehydration gives ethene.

text: Which statements about the dry cell are correct? (P) The zinc container acts as the anode. (Q) The zinc container touches the paste of MnO₂ and carbon. (R) A dry cell can be recharged easily. (S) The graphite rod acts as the cathode.
explanation: In a Leclanché dry cell, the zinc container is the anode and the graphite rod is the cathode. The zinc is in contact with the NH₄Cl/ZnCl₂ paste (the MnO₂ + carbon paste surrounds the graphite rod), and a dry cell is a primary cell — it cannot be recharged.

text: The paramagnetic metal complex ion among the following is: (Atomic numbers: Fe = 26, Cu = 29, Co = 27, Ni = 28)
explanation: Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹ and always has one unpaired electron, so [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ is paramagnetic. [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ (low-spin d⁶) and square-planar [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ (d⁸, dsp²) have all electrons paired.

text: When KMnO₄ is heated with acidified oxalic acid, gas bubbles are evolved. These are due to the formation of:
explanation: Acidified permanganate oxidises oxalic acid to carbon dioxide: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O.

text: The reaction of ethanamide with bromine and alcoholic sodium hydroxide gives:
explanation: Hofmann bromamide degradation removes one carbon: CH₃CONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → CH₃NH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O. The product is methylamine.

text: Equimolar solutions of non-volatile solutes A and B show depressions in freezing point in the ratio 2 : 1. If A remains in its normal state in solution, B is:
explanation: ΔTf ∝ i. With i(A) = 1, i(B) = 1/2 < 1, so B must be associated in solution (e.g. dimerised).

text:
Assertion: Specific conductivity of all electrolytes decreases on dilution.
Reason: On dilution, the number of ions per unit volume decreases.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Specific conductivity is the conductance of 1 cm³ of solution; on dilution there are fewer ions per cm³, so it decreases. The Reason correctly explains it. (Molar conductivity, by contrast, increases.)

text:
Assertion: Ammonolysis of alkyl halides involves the reaction between alkyl halides and alcoholic ammonia.
Reason: Ammonolysis of alkyl halides produces secondary amines only.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
explanation: Ammonolysis is heating an alkyl halide with alcoholic ammonia (Assertion true). It gives a mixture of primary, secondary and tertiary amines and the quaternary ammonium salt, not secondary amines only (Reason false).

text: Fill in the blanks: ______ is an example of a primary cell but ______ is an example of a secondary cell.
explanation: A dry (Leclanché) cell cannot be recharged — a primary cell. A nickel–cadmium cell can be recharged — a secondary cell.

text: Fill in the blanks: The complex [Ni(CO)₄] is ______ in shape and nickel is in the ______ oxidation state in it.
explanation: CO is a neutral ligand, so Ni is in the zero oxidation state (3d¹⁰ after rearrangement); sp³ hybridisation gives a tetrahedral, diamagnetic complex.

text: Fill in the blanks: When acetaldehyde is treated with hydrazine and KOH in high-boiling ethylene glycol, ______ is formed and the reaction is known as ______ reduction.
explanation: Wolff–Kishner reduction converts C=O into CH₂: CH₃CHO → (NH₂NH₂, then KOH/glycol, heat) → CH₃CH₃ (ethane).

text: Fill in the blanks: Transition metal ions having ______ d-orbitals are colourless and ______ in nature.
explanation: Ions with a completely filled d¹⁰ subshell (e.g. Zn²⁺, Cu⁺) have no d–d transitions (colourless) and no unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

text: Which of the following produces the foul-smelling compound methyl isocyanide in the presence of alcoholic KOH?
explanation: Carbylamine reaction (primary amines only): CH₃NH₂ + CHCl₃ + 3KOH → CH₃NC + 3KCl + 3H₂O. Aniline would give phenyl isocyanide; secondary amines don't react.

text: The osmotic pressure of a solution: (P) increases with an increase in the number of moles of solute; (Q) decreases with an increase in the number of moles of solute; (R) increases at a higher temperature; (S) depends on the nature of the solute. Which is correct?
explanation: π = (n/V)RT: it increases with the number of moles of solute and with temperature. Being colligative, it does not depend on the nature of the solute.

text: Which one of the following is the strongest acid?
explanation: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring, so phenol is far more acidic than aliphatic alcohols.

text: Which one of the following does NOT form a silver mirror on heating with Tollens' reagent?
explanation: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar: the glycosidic bond links the anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose, so it has no free aldehyde/ketone group.

text: The coordination number and oxidation state of the central metal D in the complex [D(en)₂(H₂O)₂]Cl₃ are:
explanation: Each en is bidentate: 2 × 2 + 2 (H₂O) = 6. The complex ion is [ ]³⁺ with neutral ligands, so D is +3.

text:
Assertion: Halogenation of benzene takes place in the presence of anhydrous FeCl₃.
Reason: Anhydrous FeCl₃ prepares a nucleophile to attack the benzene ring.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
explanation: FeCl₃ is a Lewis acid that generates the electrophile Cl⁺ (Cl₂ + FeCl₃ → Cl⁺ + FeCl₄⁻); halogenation of benzene is electrophilic substitution. So the Reason is false.

text:
Assertion: Zr and Hf have nearly the same atomic radii even though they are in different periods.
Reason: The lanthanoid contraction prevents the expected increase in the atomic radius of Hf.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
explanation: The 14 poorly-shielding 4f electrons filled before Hf cause the lanthanoid contraction, cancelling the expected size increase; so Zr (160 pm) ≈ Hf (159 pm).

text: Fill in the blanks: A mixture of anhydrous ZnCl₂ and conc. HCl is called ______ reagent, which shows maximum reactivity with ______ alcohol.
explanation: ZnCl₂ + conc. HCl is the Lucas reagent. Tertiary alcohols react fastest (immediate turbidity) because they form the most stable carbocation.

text: Fill in the blanks: Methyl chloride on treatment with ______ forms methyl cyanide, whereas on treatment with ______ it forms methyl isocyanide.
explanation: KCN is ionic, so the carbon end of CN⁻ attacks: CH₃CN. AgCN is covalent, so nitrogen attacks: CH₃NC.

text: Fill in the blanks: The hydrolysis of ethyl acetate in acidic medium is a pseudo ______ order reaction. However, the molecularity of the reaction is ______.
explanation: Water is in large excess, so rate = k′[ester] — pseudo first order — while two molecules (ester and water) take part, so molecularity is two.

text: Fill in the blanks: Dissociation of solute particles leads to a/an ______ in the magnitude of a colligative property and a/an ______ in the value of the observed molecular mass.
explanation: Dissociation increases the number of particles (i > 1), so the colligative property increases and the calculated (observed) molar mass decreases.

text: Which of the following is a tetrahedral complex as well as diamagnetic?
explanation: In [Ni(CO)₄], Ni(0) is 3d¹⁰ after rearrangement, sp³ hybridised — tetrahedral with no unpaired electrons. [NiCl₄]²⁻ is tetrahedral but paramagnetic; [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is square planar; [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ is square planar and paramagnetic.

text: When H₂S gas is passed through acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ solution, the colour of the solution changes to:
explanation: Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to green Cr³⁺ (and sulphur separates): Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3H₂S + 8H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3S + 7H₂O.

text: Identify the end product [C]: HC≡CH —dil. H₂SO₄/HgSO₄→ [A] —[O]→ [B] —PCl₅→ [C]
explanation: Hydration of ethyne gives acetaldehyde [A]; oxidation gives acetic acid [B]; PCl₅ converts –COOH to –COCl, giving acetyl chloride [C].

text: Rohit studies the iodoform reaction with (P) CH₃OH, (Q) CH₃CHO, (R) CH₃COCH₃ and (S) CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃. Which give an iodoform test when heated separately with iodine and aqueous NaOH?
explanation: The iodoform test needs a CH₃CO– group (or CH₃CH(OH)–). Acetaldehyde and acetone have it; methanol and pentan-3-one do not.

text: Which one of the following nitrogen bases is absent in RNA?
explanation: RNA contains A, G, C and U; thymine is found only in DNA (uracil replaces it in RNA).

text:
Assertion: Phenols are more acidic than aliphatic alcohols.
Reason: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance but the alkoxide ion is not.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
explanation: The negative charge of phenoxide is delocalised over the ring; the alkoxide's charge is localised on oxygen. Greater stability of the conjugate base makes phenol more acidic.

text:
Assertion: The depression of freezing point of a 0.1 molal aqueous MgCl₂ solution is less than that of a 0.1 molal aqueous NaCl solution.
Reason: The number of particles furnished by 0.1 molal MgCl₂ is less than that of 0.1 molal NaCl.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true and Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
explanation: MgCl₂ gives 3 ions (i ≈ 3) and NaCl gives 2 (i ≈ 2), so MgCl₂ furnishes more particles and shows a larger depression. Both statements are false.
